ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\angle ACD$ is an exterior angle of $\triangle ABC$, $CE$ bisects $\angle ACD$. If $\angle A=60^\circ$ and $\angle B=40^\circ$, then what is the measure of $\angle DCE$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Since $CE$ bisects $\angle ACD$, \\
it follows that $\angle ACD=2\angle ECD$, \\
since $\angle ACD$ is an exterior angle of $\triangle ABC$, \\
thus $\angle ACD=2\angle ECD=\angle A+\angle B$, \\
therefore, $2\angle DCE=60^\circ+40^\circ=100^\circ$, \\
hence, $\angle DCE=\boxed{50^\circ}$.
